newsitem.title: CHINA: Jiangxi Copper sees softer copper price.
newsitem.headline: Jiangxi Copper sees softer copper price.

text.p: Mainland copper producer Jiangxi Copper Co Ltd said on Wednesday it expected softer copper prices in July and August but its outlook remained optimistic in line with economic growth prospects in other countries.

"Consumption on copper is expected to fall in July and August," said the company's chairman He Chang Ming in a press briefing on Wednesday. He said a reduction in consumption during the period would be mainly due to holidays in European countries.

"However, as the economies of Japan, the United States, Britain and other European countries continue to grow, consumption of the metal will keep rising in the long run and copper prices can still have an upside potential," He said.

In order to tackle the possible slide in copper and gold prices which might lower the company's annual revenue, He said the company would increase production capacity, enhance sales revenue through flexible pricing and lower production costs.
Jiangxi Copper will increase the proportion of direct sales and capture optimal pricing opportunities through participation in the domestic and international metal exchanges, He said.
The company also will increase the proportion of its self-produced copper concentrates, which will effectively increase copper production capacity and lower production cost, He said.
Despite the increase in the production capacity, the company does not expect to have significant copper inventory left by the year end, He said.

He also said the company was expected to benefit from the Chinese government's 30 percent reduction in resources tax payable by mining enterprises, and an exemption from city maintenance and construction tax and education surcharges.

"In the first half, the company has met the target in production, sales and revenue. The company is confident to achieve the sales and profit target of not less than 500 million yuan for the full year," He said.
Jiangxi Copper, the first Chinese mining enterprise to be listed in Hong Kong, has reported a 230.1 million yuan profit for six months to June 30, 1997.
Its turnover was 1.48 billion yuan and earnings per share were 0.1246 yuan during the six-months period.
The company was listed on June 12, 1997.

Director Du Xingming said the company had produced 65,474 tonnes of copper cathode during the six-months period, and had sold 53,066 tonnes of copper cathode at an average price of 22,685 yuan per tonne.

Du said the company had also sold 2,535 kilograms of gold at an average price of 91,190 yuan per kilogram during the period, 27,127 kilogram of silver, 470,000 tonnes of pyrite concentrate and 260,000 tonnes of sulfuric acid.
The output of copper and gold can be increased by a big margin following the start of operations at the company's new oxygen plant in July, He said.
